My problem is the Earth husbandry literature says small birds need tighter than human: flow-through lungs, cross-current gas exchange, "more efficient extraction," therefore more sensitive to both low pO2 and contaminants. Nobody has ever quantified this in the environment we're actually building. Meanwhile the cost of believing it is a separate enclosure standard — own scrubber loop, own pressure envelope — which pencils out to roughly nine extra kilos per bird plus continuous power. At those numbers the small habitat tiers just quietly stop offering pets at all, and I don't think anyone in the room has done the math on how many families that is.

So my draft says the avian-sensitivity body of work is non-transferable pending microgravity data, and harmonizes bird enclosures to the human baseline, with a revisit trigger if operational data shows anything. Clean, defensible, saves mass, and more people get to bring a budgie.
